title: Capability mapping
description: Maps capability classes to the tool identifiers of one pinned runtime version. This schema describes the shape of that mapping and deliberately contains no runtime identifier of its own: it lives in a core path, and FR-04 confines runtime-specific names to the binding layer. A populated instance therefore belongs under core/binding/, never beside this file. The indirection is what contains the open item on unconfirmed runtime capability identifiers.

runtimeName.description: Which runtime this mapping is for. A value, supplied by the binding layer, never a constant in this contract.

runtimeVersion.description: The exact pinned version the mapping was produced against. A mapping without a version is untestable: the identifiers a runtime advertises can change between versions, so a mapping that does not say which version it describes cannot be reconciled against anything.

verificationState.description: Starts unverified and stays there until the reconciliation gate runs against the named runtime version. The source declares its capability identifiers unconfirmed, so a mapping asserted as correct without that gate would be a claim the framework cannot support. Unverified is the honest default rather than an error state.

reconciledAt.description: When the reconciliation gate last ran. Absent while the state is unverified.

reconciledCapabilitySetHash.description: The digest of the capability set the named runtime version advertised when the gate last ran, recorded per runtime version (FR-51). The timestamp says a gate ran; this says what it saw. Without it, a runtime that quietly adds a capability between two runs of the same version produces a mapping that is still stamped reconciled and no longer describes the runtime, and nothing in the document can tell the two states apart. Absent while the state is unverified, for the same reason the timestamp is.

toolListPointer.description: Where, in a binding emitted for this runtime, the explicit tool list appears. A location, never a value: this says which position in the emitted document must hold the list, and never what the list contains, so the contract stays runtime-agnostic while the check that reads it does not have to guess. Deliberately optional rather than required, because a mapping consumed only by the reconciliation gate has no use for it, and because making its absence a schema failure would move NEG-D's refusal into JSON Schema, where NEG-D's own test would prove nothing about NEG-D. Its absence is therefore refused by the explicit-tool-list check instead, which fails closed on a binding layer that does not say where the list lives (NEG-D).

toolListUnavailable.description: Declares that the named runtime accepts no explicit tool list at all, so there is no location for toolListPointer to name. Mutually exclusive with toolListPointer, and refused alongside it by the explicit-tool-list check rather than here, for the same reason that check owns the pointer's absence: moving either rule into JSON Schema would make NEG-D's own test prove nothing about NEG-D. This property exists because absence has two meanings. A mapping with no pointer because nobody has written one yet, and a mapping with no pointer because the runtime has no such concept, both fail NEG-D closed, which is correct, but only one of them is a finished piece of work and nothing in the document could tell them apart.

reason.description: What was inspected and what was found. Long enough that a bare word cannot satisfy it, because a reason nobody had to write is the same as no reason.

observedInRuntimeVersion.description: The runtime version the absence was observed in. Recorded separately from runtimeVersion so that a pin raised without re-checking leaves the two disagreeing, rather than carrying the old finding forward under the new version's name.

entries.description: Required, and required even when empty. An empty mapping maps nothing and says so. A capability the runtime advertises and this mapping does not classify fails the build rather than defaulting to allowed (NEG-C).

then.description: An unverified mapping cannot carry a reconciliation timestamp or a reconciled capability-set digest. Otherwise a stale value would read as evidence of a gate that never ran.

entries.description: A reconciled mapping that classifies nothing would mean the gate ran against the named runtime version and found no capability at all. That is indistinguishable from the gate not having run, and it is the state an empty mapping is honest about only while it is still unverified.

else.description: A reconciled mapping must say when it was reconciled and what capability set it saw, so staleness is visible rather than assumed.

schemaVersion.description: The version of this schema the instance conforms to (FR-05, FR-29). Pinned with const rather than left to the pattern: without it an instance could declare any version at all and still validate, which made the declaration decorative (NFR-21).

sha256Hex.description: Lowercase hex, exactly 64 characters, as ADR-0004 pins. Uppercase is rejected rather than folded: a digest that compares unequal to its own recomputation is the failure this field exists to detect.

jsonPointer.description: An RFC 6901 JSON Pointer with at least one reference token. The empty pointer, which denotes the whole document, is excluded: a document is not a list, so accepting it would only move the failure one step later.

identifier.description: Lowercase, hyphen-separated. Constrained so an identifier cannot carry arbitrary text, and English by construction (FR-03, CON-01).

timestamp.description: RFC 3339, UTC, Z-suffixed. The pattern is present because format is an annotation by default.

capabilityClass.description: The same closed set the tool policy and the agent definition use.

runtimeToolNames.description: The runtime's own names for the tools that realise this class. Values only: this contract states that such names exist and constrains their shape, and never enumerates one.

note.description: Why this class maps as it does, for the reviewer who has to check it against the runtime.
